title: Name the common denominator
text: 5 and 2 share no factor other than 1, so the least common denominator is their product. A common mistake is to subtract numerators and denominators to get $$\frac{3}{3}$$. What is $$5 \times 2$$?

title: Rewrite $$\frac{4}{5}$$ over 10
text: Multiply the numerator 4 by 2. What is the new numerator?

title: Rewrite $$\frac{1}{2}$$ and subtract
text: $$\frac{1}{2} = \frac{5}{10}$$. What is $$8 - 5$$, the numerator of the difference?

title: Worked solution
text: $$\frac{4}{5} - \frac{1}{2} = \frac{8}{10} - \frac{5}{10} = \frac{3}{10}$$. Common mistake: $$\frac{4 - 1}{5 - 2} = 1$$. General rule: when the denominators are different, build the least common denominator, rewrite both fractions, and only then subtract the numerators.
